method: Central difference, physical hip output scale0.25, physical position/velocity input scale1, previous physical target converted by/0.25.10-lag term-major input histories; all3 transition networks share tensor layout and units. Motion commands, reference anchor orientation, default-position subtraction and previous-action encoding are policy-specific. Evaluate all3 models on each of3 physical histories, holding measured previous physical targets fixed. Aggregate largest singular value of bilateral2x2 Jacobians, median/p95. Frequency uses frozen local kernels sum_l J_l exp(-i2pi*f*l*0.02); not motor/closed-loop frequency response.
sample_window: 45 mature-history points: nominal policy phase0.20<=t<1.10s after inferred activation,20ms intervals
scope_limits: Leg-to-Wheel and Wheel-to-Leg references have opposite motions. Same actual state acrossmodels does not make their full observation tensors identical.
Cross-task states can be outside normal deployment distribution; reciprocal comparison reduces trajectory confounding but does not prove robustness.

Oct12 logs show successful rope-free transitions, but actual test model identity was not independently captured. Near-exact reference-model replay provides consistency evidence, not independent process identity.
Latest W2L has no real rollout. All latest outputs here are offline counterfactuals with recorded prior actions.
Main window is early0.2–1.1s, not full transition or landing.
One-row reconstruction lag is not measured hardware delay.
Lower local feedback gain is not universally better; it can also weaken posture correction.
